items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: The interviewee (Johnny Wiggs) does not mention Reverend Charles Green. The interviewer mentions him only to announce a future panel discussion: 'Reverend Charles Green of the Word of Faith Temple. He's been with us before.'

ctx.x: French quadrille. I don't know how to say that big word anyway. But to me, that's the way jazz was born. There was no particular time that it was born. It was just born from these poor people with this enormous amount of gift that the black person has in almost any subject you want to mention. And that was his treatment. They still do it nowadays. You can hear some of these old-timers. Instead of playing an F sharp, they'll play an F natural, you know, and their ear won't hear. They've been doing it for 50 years,…

You know, I'd like to throw in something there. You know, you can point out the work songs and blues and the spirituals and all these things that went into jazz, and you can point out examples of European folk music or opera, different things. But one thing that we played this morning certainly is brass band-style jazz. And the brass band, being so popular in New Orleans, seems to have had a tremendous influence on the way of playing the instruments and even on the choice of the instruments themselves.…
Right in there? Somewhere around the earliest 50s, maybe 50 or something. Maybe 50.
